name: humanize
description: Human-readable numbers and times: byte sizes, durations, relative times, ordinals, plurals, lists, compact numbers, number words, Roman numerals, fractions

api.name: format_bytes
api.doc:
`n` bytes in SI units (powers of 1000: B, kB, MB, GB, TB, PB, EB) with one decimal and trailing
zeros dropped: "999 B", "1 kB", "1.5 kB", "-2.3 MB". Rounding can carry into the next unit
(999950 is "1 MB").

api.name: format_bytes_iec
api.doc:
`n` bytes in IEC units (powers of 1024: B, KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB, EiB) with one decimal and
trailing zeros dropped: "1 KiB", "1.5 MiB".

api.name: format_bytes_with
api.sig: fn format_bytes_with(n: Int, binary: Bool, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 10) -> Str
api.doc:
`n` bytes in IEC units when `binary`, else SI units, with at most `decimals` decimals (0 to 10,
trailing zeros dropped). Sizes below one kilobyte are whole bytes ("512 B").

api.name: parse_bytes
api.doc:
Parses a byte size such as "1.5 GB", "10MiB", "512", "2 kb" or "3 bytes" to a number of bytes,
rounded to the nearest byte (ties to even). Units are case-insensitive: B (or byte, bytes), the
SI units K/KB (1000), M/MB, G/GB, T/TB, P/PB, E/EB, and the IEC units KiB (1024), MiB, GiB, TiB,
PiB, EiB. `none` for an unknown unit, malformed text or a size beyond Int.

api.name: format_duration
api.doc:
Duration `d` precisely and compactly, largest unit first, zero parts left out: "1d 2h 3m 4s",
"1s 250ms", "250ms", "0ms" for zero, "-1h 30m" for a negative duration.

api.name: format_ms
api.doc: `ms` milliseconds as format_duration writes them.

api.name: format_duration_long
api.doc:
Duration `d` in words, largest unit first, zero parts left out: "1 hour, 2 minutes and 3
seconds", "250 milliseconds", "0 seconds" for zero, "minus 2 days" for a negative duration.

api.name: approximate_duration
api.doc:
Duration `d` approximately, as Rails' distance_of_time_in_words words it (the sign is ignored):
"less than a minute" (under 30 seconds), "1 minute", "5 minutes", "about 1 hour", "about 3
hours" (to 23.5 hours), "1 day", "12 days", "about 1 month", "4 months", "about 1 year",
"over 2 years", "almost 3 years". Minutes are rounded to the nearest one first.

api.name: relative_time
api.doc:
A time `d` away from now in words, where `d` is `t.since(now)`: positive is in the future and
negative in the past. Under 10 seconds either way is "just now"; otherwise it is
approximate_duration with "ago" or "in": "3 minutes ago", "in about 2 hours".

api.name: parse_duration
api.doc:
Parses a duration: one or more parts, each a number (a fraction is allowed) and a unit, with
optional spaces, commas and "and" between them: "1h30m", "90s", "1.5h", "250ms", "2 days, 3
hours and 4 minutes", "-1h". Units: ms (msec, millisecond), s (sec, second), m (min, minute),
h (hr, hour), d (day), w (wk, week), singular or plural, case-insensitive. The total is rounded
to the nearest millisecond (ties to even). `none` for a bare number, an unknown unit or a
total beyond Int.

api.name: ordinal_suffix
api.doc:
The English ordinal suffix of `n`: "st", "nd", "rd" or "th" (11, 12 and 13 take "th", as do
111, 112 and 113). The sign is ignored.

api.name: ordinal
api.doc:
`n` with its ordinal suffix: "1st", "2nd", "3rd", "11th", "21st", "111th", "-1st" (a negative
number keeps its sign and takes the suffix of its magnitude).

api.name: pluralize
api.doc:
The plural of English noun `word`: irregular nouns ("person" to "people", "child" to
"children", "leaf" to "leaves", "analysis" to "analyses", "cactus" to "cacti"), uncountable
ones unchanged ("sheep", "information"), then the rules for "-y" after a consonant ("-ies"),
"-s -x -z -ch -sh" ("-es") and otherwise "-s". The case of `word` is kept: "Box" gives "Boxes"
and "BOX" gives "BOXES". An empty word stays empty.

api.name: singularize
api.doc:
The singular of English noun `word`, undoing pluralize: irregular plurals ("people", "mice",
"wolves", "crises"), uncountable nouns unchanged, then "-ies" to "-y", "-sses" to "-ss",
"-xes -zes -ches -shes" without "-es", and a final "-s" dropped unless the word ends in "ss",
"us" or "is". A word that is already singular is returned unchanged where the rules can tell.
The case of `word` is kept.

api.name: plural_for
api.sig: fn plural_for(n: Int, word: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `word` if `n` is 1 (or -1), else its plural.

api.name: count_noun
api.sig: fn count_noun(n: Int, word: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `n` and the noun, with thousands separators: "1 file", "0 files", "1,234 files", "-1 file".

api.name: quantity
api.sig: fn quantity(n: Int, word: Str) -> Str
api.doc: Like count_noun but zero is "no": "no files", "1 file", "3 files".

api.name: join_list
api.doc:
The items joined as an English list with "and" and no serial comma: "" for none, "a", "a and
b", "a, b and c".

api.name: join_list_oxford
api.doc: The items joined with "and" and the serial (Oxford) comma: "a, b, and c" ("a and b" for two).

api.name: join_or
api.doc: The items joined with "or": "a, b or c".

api.name: join_words
api.sig: fn join_words(xs: List[Str], conj: Str, oxford: Bool) -> Str
api.doc:
The items joined with commas and conjunction `conj` before the last one, with a comma before
it too when `oxford` and there are at least three items.

api.name: join_truncated
api.sig: fn join_truncated(xs: List[Str], limit: Int where _ >= 0) -> Str
api.doc:
The first `limit` items and a count of the rest: "a, b and 3 others" ("and 1 other"); all of
them as join_list when there are at most `limit`. With `limit` 0 only the count is left
("5 others").

api.name: with_commas
api.doc: `n` with commas between groups of three digits: "1,234,567", "-1,000".

api.name: group_digits
api.sig: fn group_digits(n: Int, sep: Str) -> Str
api.doc: `n` with `sep` between groups of three digits: group_digits(1234567, " ") is "1 234 567".

api.name: with_commas_f64
api.sig: fn with_commas_f64(x: F64, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 20) -> Str
api.doc:
`x` with commas between groups of three digits and exactly `decimals` decimals:
"1,234.57". NaN and infinities are written "nan", "inf" and "-inf".

api.name: compact
api.doc:
`n` in short compact form with one decimal at most: "999", "1.2k", "3.4M", "1.2B", "1T",
"-1.5k". The value is rounded half away from zero, and rounding can carry into the next unit
(999950 is "1M", 999949 is "999.9k"). Above 999.95 trillion it stays in trillions with
separators ("9,223,372T").

api.name: compact_long
api.doc: `n` in long compact form: "1.2 thousand", "3.4 million", "1 billion", "2 trillion".

api.name: compact_with
api.sig: fn compact_with(n: Int, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 6, long: Bool) -> Str
api.doc:
`n` in compact form with at most `decimals` decimals (trailing zeros dropped), short ("1.23k")
or `long` ("1.23 thousand").

api.name: parse_compact
api.doc:
Parses a compact number back to an Int: "1.2k" (1200), "3.4M", "1.5 billion", "2T", "-1,500",
"750". Suffixes are case-insensitive: k or thousand, m or million, b, bn or billion, t, tn or
trillion. The value is rounded to the nearest integer (ties to even). `none` for malformed text,
an unknown suffix or a value beyond Int.

api.name: number_words
api.doc:
`n` in English words, in the US style without "and": "zero", "seven", "forty-two",
"one hundred twenty-three", "minus five", "one million two thousand three". Every Int works,
up to the quintillions of the smallest one.

api.name: ordinal_words
api.doc:
`n` as an English ordinal in words: "first", "second", "twelfth", "twenty-first",
"one hundredth", "one million second", "minus third".

api.name: apnumber
api.doc:
`n` in Associated Press style: words for 0 to 9 ("zero" to "nine"), digits otherwise ("10",
"-3").

api.name: to_roman
api.sig: fn to_roman(n: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 3999) -> Str
api.doc:
`n` as a Roman numeral in the standard subtractive form: 4 is "IV", 1994 is "MCMXCIV", 3999 is
"MMMCMXCIX".

api.name: from_roman
api.doc:
Parses a Roman numeral in the standard form to_roman writes, upper case only: "XIV" is 14.
Non-standard forms ("IIII", "IC", "VX", "MMMM") and anything else give `none`.

api.name: percent
api.sig: fn percent(x: F64, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 20) -> Str
api.doc: The ratio `x` as a percentage with exactly `decimals` decimals: percent(0.125, 1) is "12.5%".

api.name: percent_of
api.sig: fn percent_of(part: Int, whole: Int where _ != 0, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 20) -> Str
api.doc:
`part` of `whole` as a percentage with exactly `decimals` decimals: percent_of(1, 3, 1) is
"33.3%".

api.name: fraction_parts
api.sig: fn fraction_parts(x: F64, max_den: Int where _ >= 1) -> (Int, Int)
api.doc:
The fraction closest to `x` whose denominator is at most `max_den`, as (numerator, denominator)
in lowest terms with a positive denominator: fraction_parts(0.75, 100) is (3, 4),
fraction_parts(3.14159, 10) is (22, 7).

api.name: fraction
api.sig: fn fraction(x: F64, max_den: Int where _ >= 1) -> Str
api.doc:
`x` as a mixed fraction with denominator at most `max_den`: "1/2", "1 1/2", "-2 3/4", "3" for a
whole number, "0" for values that round to zero.

api.name: scientific
api.sig: fn scientific(x: F64, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 20) -> Str
api.doc:
`x` in scientific notation with `decimals` decimals in the mantissa and a superscript
exponent: scientific(12345.0, 2) is "1.23 x 10⁴", scientific(0.00042, 1) is "4.2 x 10⁻⁴". NaN
and infinities are written "nan", "inf" and "-inf".

api.name: metric
api.sig: fn metric(x: F64, unit: Str, decimals: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 20) -> Str
api.doc:
`x` with an SI prefix for `unit` and `decimals` decimals (trailing zeros dropped): metric(1500.0,
"V", 2) is "1.5 kV", metric(0.000002, "F", 1) is "2 µF". Prefixes run from y (10^-24) to Y
(10^24); rounding can carry into the next prefix (999.96 with one decimal is "1 k"). Zero is
"0 " plus the unit; NaN and infinities are written "nan", "inf" and "-inf" before the unit.
